item.title: Sri Lanka’s new budget motivates students’ investment in risky assets
item.dc:creator: Shihar Aneez
item.description: Most Sri Lankans still invest in risk-free fixed assets
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka’s 2027 budget has proposed to provide a share portfolio subject to a maximum of Rs. 10,000 to boost investment into risky assets of share market, the official 2027 budget document showed.

The number of persons actively trading in connection with the Colombo Stock Exchange is only around 0.7 percent of the population over 18 years of age, the document said.

The government has proposed to implement a new programme named “A Share for Everyone” under the vision “Let’s Know, Let’s Learn, Let’s Invest”.

“With the aim of actively connecting students in schools who are studying for the Advanced Level in Grade 13 and are over 18 years of age with the stock market, it is proposed to introduce the project to provide a share portfolio subject to a maximum of Rs. 10,000/-, in accordance with a formal selection procedure,” the government said.

President Anura Kumara Dissanayake in his capacity as the finance minister also proposed to introduce a mechanism to encourage small and medium-scale enterprises to get listed in the Colombo Stock Exchange. (Colombo/November 12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka rupee closes at 332.50/60 to US dollar spot, bond yields down
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: Bond yields closed steeply lower, dealers said.
item.content:encoded:

A bond maturing on 15.10.2034 closed at 11.82/87 percent, down from 11.93/97 percent.

item.title: Sri Lanka cuts import taxes on 3 essential foods, raises levy on sugar
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: The tax cuts on these foods will take effect from November 13, Dissanayake told parliament on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka has slashed import taxes on sprats, Maldive fish and dried chillies, while raising the levy on imported sugar by 10 rupees a kilogram, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said presenting the 2027 budget.

The tax cuts on these foods will take effect from November 13, Dissanayake told parliament on Thursday.

Under the proposals, the Special Commodity Levy on imported sprats will drop from 100 rupees to 10 rupees a kilogram, while the levy on Maldive fish will be cut from 302 rupees to 10 rupees a kilogram.

The Special Commodity Levy on both powdered and whole dried chillies will also be reduced by 50 rupees a kilogram.

“We propose to reduce the Special Commodity Levy to ease the cost-of-living pressure faced by consumers due to rising prices of essential food items,” Dissanayake told parliament.

The government proposed increasing the Special Commodity Levy on imported sugar by 10 rupees a kilogram to help local sugar producers compete on equal terms.

“To protect the local sugar industry and reduce the tax gap with imported sugar, we propose increasing the levy on imported sugar by 10 rupees a kilogram,” he said.

While cutting duties on sprats, Maldive fish and dried chillies reduces tax collection on those staples, budget estimates show the combined Special Commodity Levy revisions will result in a net annual revenue gain of 950 million rupees rather than an overall loss, once the higher tax on imported sugar is factored in.

The budget’s revenue impact summary lists November 2026 as the effective start for the Special Commodity Levy revisions.

The food tax relief comes as consumers have faced renewed price pressures, with annual inflation rising to 8.3 percent by October 2026 following higher fuel costs linked to conflict in West Asia.  (Colombo/Nov12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka to forego Rs.28.4bn in next year on income tax, CESS, VAT revisions
item.dc:creator: Shihar Aneez
item.description: Income tax revision will see Rs.16bn loss for state
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka will see a loss of Rs. 28.4 billion in its revenue next year due to revisions in income tax, Port and Airports Development Levy (PAL), Value Added Tax (VAT), and removal of CESS, the 2027 budget document showed.

The government will lose Rs. 16 billion from new tax structure that will see a rise in tax free income, Rs. 10 billion due to removal of CESS, and Rs. 2.98 billion from the revision of VAT.

The government will also lose Rs. 350 million from the revision in PAL and Rs. 40 million from abolition of Tourism Development Levy.

It will only see a gain of Rs.950 million from the revision in Special Commodity Levy. (Colombo/November 12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka to cut CESS on 800 import items by 25-pct, scrap PAL on newsprint, solar batteries
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: CESS cut will result in an annual revenue loss of 10,000 million rupees, while changes to PAL will cost the state 350 mn
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka will slash existing CESS import taxes on 800 selected product categories by 25 per cent from April 2027 and remove the Ports and Airports Development Levy (PAL) on imported newsprint and solar storage batteries from January 2027, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said.

Presenting the 2027 budget in Parliament on Thursday, Dissanayake outlined the tariff changes as part of wider tax policy reforms.

According to official budget revenue estimates, the CESS cut will result in an annual revenue loss of 10,000 million rupees, while changes to PAL will cost the state 350 million rupees a year.

The 25 per cent reduction in CESS covers 800 selected Harmonized System (HS) customs code lines and marks the second phase of the government’s programme to gradually remove import tariffs.

“To simplify the import tax structure, reduce trade costs, and boost economic competitiveness, I propose cutting existing CESS rates on 800 selected HS code lines by 25 per cent,” Dissanayake told Parliament.

Alongside the CESS reduction, the government will scrap the existing 10 per cent PAL currently charged on imported newspaper printing paper classified under specified HS codes.

“I propose removing the existing 10 per cent Ports and Airports Development Levy currently charged on the import of newsprint under specified HS codes, effective January 1, 2027,” he said.

The budget also proposes abolishing PAL on imported batteries used for storing solar energy.

This tax relief accompanies a new subsidy of 25,000 rupees per kilowatt-hour—up to a maximum of 250,000 rupees for 10 kilowatt-hours—for households installing rooftop solar systems with battery storage under the Net Plus scheme to promote renewable power and stabilize the national grid.

According to the government’s 2027 revenue impact summary, the 350 million rupee annual revenue loss from the PAL revisions will take effect in January 2027, followed by the 10,000 million rupee annual loss from the second phase of CESS cuts in April 2027, forming part of an overall 28,415 million rupee annual revenue loss across all proposed budget tax changes. (Colombo/Nov12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka’s national budget 2027 promises tax relief, capital spending
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: The English transcript of the full 2027 budget speech is available here:
item.content:encoded:
ECONMYNEXT – Sri Lanka President Anura Kumara Dissanayake, in his capacity as Minister of Finance, presented the 2027 National Budget to Parliament on Thursday.

The third budget of the National People’s Power (NPP) administration seeks to boost production, attract foreign investment, and ease cost-of-living pressures while maintaining fiscal discipline ahead of the conclusion of Sri Lanka’s International Monetary Fund (IMF) Extended Fund Facility in March 2027.

The English transcript of the full 2027 budget speech is available here:

(Colombo/Nov12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka to exempt books from value added tax: President
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: Exercise books and printed books
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka will exempt exercise books and printed books from value added tax (VAT), President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said in his 2027 national budget speech.

Printed books and other printed materials became subject to VAT effective from January 2024, while exercise books had been subject to VAT before that, Dissanayake told parliament.

“Recognizing the importance of education and the necessity of ensuring that essential educational materials are available at an affordable price, and with the objective of promoting access to education, knowledge and reading, we propose to exempt textbooks, dictionaries, encyclopaedias, children’s drawing and colouring books, educational publications and other printed books, as well as exercise books, from Value Added Tax (VAT).” (Colombo/Nov12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka relaxes personal income tax threshold in 2027 budget
item.dc:creator: Shihar Aneez
item.description: The maximum 36% tax rate applies for annual income of above Rs.5.2mn
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka will revise the income tax rate structure with a relaxed threshold, increasing the annual taxable income to Rs.1.95 million from the current Rs. 1.8 million, the 2027 budget document showed.

Under the revised structure, the 6% personal tax rate applies to income above Rs. 850,000 after the annual income of Rs.1.95 million.

The new structure will see the personal tax income rate reaching maximum 36 percent for an annual income of Rs. 5.2 million instead of the current Rs. 4.3 million.

The government expects 16 billion rupees loss due to the income tax revisions. (Colombo/November 12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka to waive dual citizenship fees for spouses, children under heritage program
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka will stop charging dual citizenship fees for the spouses, second-generation children, and third-generation children of applicants under a new Global Sri Lankan Heritage Citizenship program, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said. Presenting the 2027 budget speech under the IMF program, Dissanayake proposed granting fee-free dual citizenship to the children of dual citizenship […]
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka will stop charging dual citizenship fees for the spouses, second-generation children, and third-generation children of applicants under a new Global Sri Lankan Heritage Citizenship program, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said.

Presenting the 2027 budget speech under the IMF program, Dissanayake proposed granting fee-free dual citizenship to the children of dual citizenship applicants as well as third-generation children of Sri Lankan origin living overseas.

“We will only collect the fee from the main applicant; we will not charge any fee at all for the rest—starting from the spouse, to the second generation and the third generation,” Dissanayake said.

Previously, fees were charged for those family members. The government is launching the Global Sri Lankan Heritage Citizenship program to remove those charges and collect a fee only from the main applicant.

The program aims to bring the skills, knowledge, and connection of Sri Lankans living abroad and their children into the country’s future development.

“We must adopt a new approach in order to integrate the knowledge and capabilities, as well as the bond with the motherland, of Sri Lankans living abroad and their children,” he said. (Colombo/Nov12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka allocates Rs800mn for Bimsaviya, Rs140mn for land digitization
item.dc:creator: Ranul Seneviratne
item.description: Plans to integrate plans of 3.5mn land parcels, which exist as hard copies with Survey Dept into land information system
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka has allocated 800 million rupees to strengthen the Bimsaviya program and 140 million rupees to modernize land records in the 2027 budget.

President Anura Kumara Dissanayake announced the funding while presenting the budget speech for the year 2027 under the IMF program.

“140 million rupees has been allocated for registering land titles, digitizing land records, and modernizing land information systems,” President Dissanayake said.

The government also plans to integrate the plans of 3.5 million land parcels — which exist as hard copies with the Government Survey Department — into its land information systems, if the plans are ready.

“We are ready to allocate the necessary provisions in the year 2027 to digitize the relevant plans of 3.5 million land parcels,” Dissanayake said. (Colombo/Nov12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka bourse gains 0.56-pct amid 2027 budget speech
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: Lifted by telcos
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka’s bourse closed up 0.56 percent on Thursday as President Anura Kumara Dissanayake was presenting the national budget for 2027.

The benchmark All Share Price Index was up 124.47 points at 22,157.40.

The more liquid S&P SL20 was up 0.26 percent, or 16.57 points at 6,365.57.

Market turnover was 2.97 billion rupees.

Top positive contributors to the ASPI were Sri Lanka Telecom (up 6.90 rupees at 92), Distilleries (up 60 cents at 58 rupees) and Dialog (up 30 cents at 50 rupees).

Sri Lanka will give a 5-year tax break on telco tower constructions and cash grants to promote wider coverage in rural areas, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said in his budget speech.

Top negative contributors were Ceylon Cold Stores (down 1.25 rupees at 125), PGP Glas (down 70 cents at 58.80 rupees) and Softlogic Capital (down 30 cents at 11.30 rupees).

The budget is anchored by a record 2,000 billion rupees (2 trillion) allocation for public capital expenditure, and includes concessions and subsidies to encourage the installation of solar power battery storage systems. (Colombo/Nov12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka abolishes Tourism Development Levy from next year
item.dc:creator: Shihar Aneez
item.description: TDL ranged from 0.5-1% depending on turnover
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka will abolish Tourism Development Levy (TDL) Tourism Development Levy (TDL) imposed under the Finance Act with effect from April 01, 2027, the country’s budget document showed.

The TDL generated Rs. 2.58 billion in 2024 and the levy was imposed to support community-focused tourism development, strategic marketing, and infrastructure improvements, ensuring sustainable growth of the sector while enhancing Sri Lanka’s global tourism brand.

The TDL is charged at 1% or 0.5% on the liable turnover of businesses registered with the Sri Lanka Tourism Development Authority (SLTDA), depending on the establishment’s revenue threshold:

A standard rate of 1.0% charged on SLTDA-licensed institutions with an annual turnover exceeding Rs. 12 million and a 0.5% charged on SLTDA-licensed institutions with an annual turnover not exceeding Rs. 12 million. (Colombo/November 12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka to build domestic flight terminal at BIA: President
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: "Jaffna citizens tell us that it takes longer for them to travel to Jaffna from Colombo than to come to Colombo from abr
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka will allocate 800 million rupees to build a domestic flight terminal within its Bandaranaike International Airport, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said in his budget speech.

“Jaffna citizens tell us that it takes longer for them to travel to Jaffna from Colombo than to come to Colombo from the country they are in,” Dissanayake told parliament.

“So we need a domestic flight terminal at Katunayake. We will begin this next year.”

The BIA currently has a domestic terminal, though it is primarily used for small air taxis.

Most domestic commercial flights operate out of the Colombo International Airport in Ratmalana. (Colombo/Nov12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka to enter expanded economic partnership with UAE, Oman: President
item.dc:creator: Shihar Aneez
item.description: Expanding FTA with India and FTA with China are also looked into
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka will enter into Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreements with the United Arab Emirates and Oman to boost trade, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake told parliament while presenting the 2027 budget.

He said the government expects to update existing free trade agreements and enter into new trade agreements with more states to connect Sri Lanka to the global trade network.

“To expand the existing free trade agreement with India, the Cabinet of Ministers has already appointed a committee of officials. Attention has been directed toward a new free trade agreement with China. An application has been made to join the Regional Comprehensive Economic Partnership (RCDEP).

“We hope to enter into Comprehensive Economic Partnership Agreements with the United Arab Emirates and Oman.”

He also said the government will implement the Sri Lanka–European Union Sustainable Trade and Economic Integration Project during the 2027–2030 period under a European Union grant of 3,430 million rupees to promote export competitiveness, export diversification, and sustainable production.

“So, we can build a very close relationship with the European market… Furthermore, following a feasibility study, we will work toward entering into new free trade agreements with other countries,” he said. (Colombo/November 12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka offers 5-year tax break, grants for rural telco towers
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: "There is a need for 700-800 new towers to enable high speed broadband internet in rural villages," Dissanayake told par
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka will give a 5-year tax break on telco tower constructions to promote wider coverage in rural areas, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said in his budget speech.

“There is a need for 700-800 new towers to enable high speed broadband internet in rural villages,” Dissanayake told parliament on Thursday.

573 are being built under this program he said.

“For each new tower constructed, 75 percent of the cost or 35 million rupees, whichever is lesser, will be given as a grant.

“Why are we giving money to the private sector for building towers, they’ll ask, Why are we giving money?

“The private sector prioritizes building towers in places with a higher population density. But they don’t build in areas where there is lower population density.

“Then rural villages don’t get coverage. So we must give concessions.”

This will be done in 3 ways he said; 1) 5-year tax break 2) Of the construction cost either 75 percent or 35 million rupees, whichever is lesser will be given 3) 5 million rupees will be given for establishing electricity connections.

“Some places will be on top of hills, so they have to draw lines.”

The goal was to establish broadband coverage in all areas of the country by 2030 he said. (Colombo/Nov12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka 2027 budget proposes subsidies for solar power battery installation
item.dc:creator: Shihar Aneez
item.description: Sri Lanka hopes to increase contribution from renewable energy to 69% by 2029 from current 62%
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka President Anura Kumara Dissanayake announced a subsidy of up to Rs. 250,000 for battery storage capacity in rooftop solar power systems in the 2027 budget.

“We are giving a subsidy to domestic users if they install a battery. To domestic consumers newly installing rooftop solar power systems, we are granting a subsidy of 25,000 rupees per kilowatt of battery storage capacity,” he told while presenting the 2027 budget in parliament.

“We propose to grant this subsidy up to 10 kilowatts, to a maximum of Rs. 250,000. We propose to allocate 3,500 million rupees for this purpose.”

He also proposed to remove the Ports and Airports Development Levy (PAL) charged upon importation for batteries used for storing solar energy.

“There is a Ports and Airports service levy of 10%. We are removing that tax for batteries. Then on a one-megawatt battery, there is a tax of approximately between 4,000 and 5,000 rupees. We are giving a subsidy of 25,000 rupees. From the tax removal, a benefit of 4,000 to 5,000 rupees is gained.”

“That means for those who install a one- -kilowatt battery, [they receive] 30,000 rupees – 25,000 as a subsidy, and an amount between 4,000 and 5,000.”

“We must move toward batteries. If we don’t move in that direction, this cannot be transformed.” (Colombo/November 12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka in process to reduce delays in allocating lands for key projects
item.dc:creator: Shihar Aneez
item.description: President says a committee appointed to fast track approvals
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka is in the process of reducing the delays in allocating lands for key projects with an aim to reduce the gap between urban-centred and rural economy, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake told the parliament while presenting the 2027 budget.

“In order to minimize the delays that occur when allocating state land, and to submit recommendations for the concessions that should be granted based on the national importance of the project,” he said.

Dissanayake said the move will help to generate number of jobs and boost investments and a committee of officials has been appointed by the Cabinet of Ministers.

“If someone investing in Colombo and someone investing in Jaffna or Polonnaruwa have the exact same privileges and concessions, they prefer to invest in Colombo.”

“If they invest in outstation provinces, looking at the scale of the investment, the number of jobs generated, and the region where the investment is carried out, we are working to provide a special concession package to those investors.”

“Only if that happens will we be able to push this Colombo urban-centered economy out to the villages.” (Colombo/November 12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka to award 4 contracts for Mannar basin oil exploration after Feb 2: President
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: "It was reported that very good companies have bid," he said in parliament on Thursday.
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka plans to award four contracts for investors to explore oil and gas in the Northwestern Mannar Basin soon after the bid deadline closes on February 2, 2027, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake said in his budget speech.

“It was reported that very good companies have bid,” he said in parliament on Thursday.

Sri Lanka has offered four offshore blocks in the Northwestern Mannar Basin for international investors to explore oil and gas in a fresh attempt to attract investments into the sector after an earlier attempt ended in a failure due to not commercially viable production.

The Mannar Basin, which lies between southern India and northwestern Sri Lanka, may hold around $260 billion worth of oil and gas resources, A Sri Lanka’s former energy minister has told the parliament in 2021.

Sri Lanka’s pursuit of offshore oil and gas exploration began in the late 1960s, initially focusing on shallow offshore areas in the Gulf of Mannar and the Cauvery Basin. (Colombo/Nov12/2026)

item.title: Sri Lanka panel explores if another IMF deal needed: President
item.dc:creator: Shihar Aneez
item.description: Current EFF ends in March 2027
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka is exploring whether the country needs another IMF deal and what kind of programme it should pursue, President Anura Kumara Dissanayake told parliament while presenting the 2027 budget.

The Extended Fund Facility (EFF) programme entered with the International Monetary Fund is scheduled to conclude in March next year.

“We hope to successfully complete the 17th IMF program. While the program to stabilize the economy domestically is proceeding successfully, at a time when we are preparing for economic transformation toward growth, it is difficult to predict the impacts caused by global and natural disasters,” he said.

“We believe our reserves must be further strengthened to successfully face such situations. Therefore, after concluding the current IMF program, the Cabinet of Ministers has appointed a committee chaired by the Deputy Minister of Finance and Planning to examine the suitability of entering another program and what kind of program to pursue, and to submit a report.”

“The committee comprising the Governor of the Central Bank, the Secretary to the Ministry of Finance, and economic experts has been appointed to examine whether we should pursue a program after March, and if so, what kind of program it should be.”

President’s comments come amid criticism over the government economic policies with critics say they have failed to spur economic growth so far. (Colombo/Nov12/2026)

item.title: Supreme Court clears Sri Lanka’s terrorism bill subject to amendments
item.dc:creator: Nirmalie Alahakone
item.description: Three of them have already been undertaken by the Additional Solicitor General at the committee stage.
item.content:encoded:
ECONOMYNEXT – Sri Lanka’s Supreme Court has determined that the Protection of the State from Terrorism Bill can be passed with a simple majority in the parliament after making the following amendments.

“Clause 26.2 to be amended by inserting the phrase ‘on the application of such police officer’; with the above insertion, clause 26.2 must read as follows:

Upon production of a suspect before magistrate under subsection 1, where the police officer conducting the investigation has reasonable grounds to believe that further extended custody of the suspect is necessary for the purpose of conducting further investigation the magistrate may on the application of such police officer for reasons to be recorded in writing authorise such suspect to be held in police custody for a further period not exceeding 24 hours.

Clause 59.5.B to be amended by substituting the phrase ‘Court of Appeal’ with the ‘Supreme Court’ to make the judicial oversight effective.

Removal of the clause 60 subclause 7 from the bill on the basis that it is superfluous; and clause 66.1 to be reframed as follows:

An executive order: Directives or directions issued under this act may be questioned under proceedings article 126, 140 or 141 of the Constitution.

I order that the full determination of the supreme court be printed of the official report of the day’s proceedings.”

Speaker Jagath Wickramaratne said that three of them have already been undertaken by the Additional Solicitor General at the committee stage. (Colombo/Nov12/2026)
